text:
The corrupted element is most likely **M5**, the tail current source. Its branch carries 68.3 µA, and the total supply current (M5 + M6 + M8 ≈ 68.3 + 10 + 35.6 ≈ 113.8 µA × 1.8 V ≈ 205 µW) explains the power failure. M5 is also the only device whose operating point is clearly wrong: it is in triode (Vds = 0.184 V < Vdsat = 0.546 V), so it no longer acts as a current source. Its effective width (W·m = 6.06 µm) is about 12× the reference M6 (0.49 µm), so the mirror ratio is far larger than a saturated tail would need. The oversized, triode-biased tail draws too much current, and the input pair's common-mode headroom is compromised. Power is also most sensitive to M5 among the candidates (+10% for a +20% change), which points to it as the source.

```json
{"ranking": ["M5", "M6", "M8"], "fault": "Tail current source M5 is oversized (m=3, effective W=6.06 um vs. M6 reference 0.49 um, ratio ~12x). The excess mirror ratio drives M5 into triode (Vds=0.184 V < Vdsat=0.546 V), so it draws ~68 uA instead of a saturated tail current. This pushes total supply current to ~114 uA (~205 uW, over the 180 uW limit). Fix: reduce M5 to m=1 (ratio ~4x) or otherwise lower its width so it operates in saturation at a current that meets the power budget."}
```
